sections.h2: What makes selling a house in Bristol, TN different?
sections.html:
Bristol is a Sullivan County city that shares a state line, a main street and a regional economy with Bristol, Virginia, with State Street as the dividing line. The two cities keep separate governments, police departments and libraries, so a Tennessee seller deals with Tennessee offices only.

The Census Bureau puts the July 1, 2025 estimate at 28,107 residents, up 3.7 percent from the 2020 base. Owners occupy 67.4 percent of homes and the median home value is $194,500, a fraction of what Brentwood or Chattanooga show. With prices at that level, a few thousand dollars of repairs or back taxes changes the net result noticeably, so compare offers by what you keep after closing.

Bristol is a principal city in the Kingsport to Bristol metro area and the wider Tri-Cities region. Bristol Motor Speedway, a NASCAR track, and the Bristol Rhythm and Roots Reunion each September bring visitors, though neither sets what an ordinary house is worth.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Bristol housing?
sections.html:
They show an older, lower-cost market with a large renter share. About 19.5 percent of residents are 65 or older, and the median household income is $58,162. Median gross rent is $842 a month.

sections.h2: How are Bristol property taxes set after the 2025 reappraisal?
sections.html:
Bristol residents pay two bills in one: Sullivan County and the City of Bristol, Tennessee. For tax year 2025 the county commission held its rate at $1.6129 per $100 of assessed value and the city council adopted $1.87, according to a January 2026 county newsletter. That adds up to $3.4829 per $100 for a house inside the city.

The reappraisal reset values, so the state certified a revenue-neutral city rate of $1.5397. The council chose $1.87, which the county calculates as 21.45 percent above that certified level. The 2024 city rate had been $2.25 on the older values.

The county assessor runs a countywide reappraisal every two years, and the next is scheduled for 2027. For a house valued at $194,500, residential assessment at 25 percent gives $48,625 of assessed value, which at $3.4829 per $100 is roughly $1,694 a year. Use your own notice for the exact amount.

sections.h2: Where do I pay Sullivan County taxes and what relief exists?
sections.html:
Taxes for 2025 were payable through the last day of February 2026, and the Trustee's main office is at 3411 Highway 126, Suite 104, Blountville, phone 423-323-6464. A Bristol office operates on Thursdays and Fridays from October 1 through March 13 at the Ralph Harr Justice Center, 801 Anderson Street, Room 139, phone 423-354-7037.

The county also runs a payment plan that splits an expected bill into ten equal monthly payments beginning in March. The same newsletter describes the state's tax relief program for older, disabled and veteran homeowners. For 2025 taxes the income cap was $37,530 based on 2024 income, with an additional $85 rebate from the county for elderly and disabled participants.

  • Homeowners older than 65 can qualify if combined income, including a spouse or co-owner, is within the cap.
  • Disabled homeowners recognized by the Social Security Administration use the same income cap.
  • Permanently and totally disabled veterans, and their surviving spouses, qualify without that cap.

Ask the Trustee which year's limits apply before you file.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Sullivan County assessment?
sections.html:
Start by contacting the assessor, Donna Whitaker, at 3411 Highway 126, Suite 103, Blountville, phone 423-323-6455, then move to the county board of equalization if the answer does not satisfy you. The assessor's page notes that the office does not set the tax rate, send the bill or collect payment, so a rate complaint goes elsewhere.

The state's appeal guide says a dispute generally has to reach the county board first. If you disagree with that decision, the state board filing is due by August 1 of the tax year or 45 days after notice of the local ruling, whichever is later. Hearings before an administrative judge turn on evidence, and the guide names comparable sales as the best proof for a house.

Pay the undisputed part of the tax by the delinquency date while an appeal is pending, since the state says unpaid amounts can bring penalties or a dismissal.

sections.h2: What local housing news affects Bristol sellers?
sections.html:
Council notices show where the city is steering development. In March 2026 the council held a public hearing on an ordinance for a temporary moratorium on establishing permanent campgrounds, and it took up a resolution supporting a workforce housing development to be built by DP Builders. Those items appear on the city's legal notices page, which also posts hearings on budgets and tax rates.

Bristol Tennessee City Schools serves nearly all of the city, with Tennessee High School as its public high school, and a small section falls under Sullivan County Schools. King University is a Bristol institution. The city's weather runs cooler than most of Tennessee: about 41 inches of precipitation a year and an average of 13.3 inches of snow, with 17 days at or above 90 degrees. Roofs, gutters and heating systems take the most wear in that range, and a lender-backed buyer may ask for repairs before closing.

For zoning questions on a particular lot, call the Department of Development Services before you plan a rental or an addition, since use rules differ by district.

sections.h2: How is a Bristol sale recorded and taxed?
sections.html:
The deed goes to the Sullivan County Register of Deeds in Blountville at 3411 Highway 126, Suite 101, phone 423-323-6420, open 8:00 am to 4:30 pm on weekdays. Tennessee's realty transfer tax is $0.37 per $100 of price, per the Department of Revenue.

Ask the title company to prorate the year's property tax on the closing statement.

  • Collect the payoff letter from every lienholder before the closing date.
  • Confirm who signs for any estate or co-owner situation.
  • Check the Trustee's record for unpaid prior-year taxes, which the title company will expect to see settled at closing.

faqs.q: How much is the Bristol, TN property tax rate?
faqs.a: For tax year 2025 the city rate is $1.87 per $100 of assessed value and the county rate is $1.6129, a combined $3.4829. Both come from the county's January 2026 newsletter. Check the current figures with the Trustee because rates are set each year.

faqs.q: When are Sullivan County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payment for 2025 taxes was due by the last day of February 2026, and the county's usual cycle is the same. The Trustee's office in Blountville can be reached at 423-323-6464. Ask the Trustee for the interest schedule on late payments.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bristol house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company normally pays any unpaid taxes out of the sale proceeds at closing. Get a current balance from the Sullivan County Trustee before you set a closing date.

faqs.q: Where is the Bristol Tennessee Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is in the county courthouse complex at 3411 Highway 126, Suite 101, Blountville. The phone number is 423-323-6420. It is open 8:00 am to 4:30 pm Monday through Friday except designated holidays.

faqs.q: Is Bristol, Tennessee the same as Bristol, Virginia?
faqs.a: No. They are two cities with separate governments that share a border at State Street. A house on the Tennessee side uses Sullivan County offices, Tennessee law and Tennessee taxes.
